gh pr create --repo punt-labs/beadle --base main --head fix/gpg-signature-verification --title "feat(daemon): implement real GPG signature verification (DES-034)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Closes beadle-iru. Replaces `internal/daemon/command.go`'s hard-coded `VerifySignature` no-op (`return nil`) with a real GPG signature verification implementation per DES-034, following the full ethos mission workflow: two-round design review, implementation, coverage audit, code-quality review, and three follow-up rounds closing gaps found by full-diff pre-PR review (missions m-2026-08-30-005 through m-2026-08-30-014, all in the mission log).

- **`internal/daemon/signature.go`** (new): `VerifySignature(cmd *Command, gpgBinary, ownerKeyID string) error` — canonical-subset signing (`CanonicalCommandBytes`), isolated single-key GNUPGHOME verification with a post-import uniqueness assertion, GnuPG `--status-fd` machine-readable classification (`LC_ALL=C` pinned, not locale-dependent stderr matching), and a `SignatureError`/`SignatureReason` type distinguishing missing/invalid/wrong-key/expired-key outcomes.
- **`internal/pgp/expiry.go`**: `CheckKeyExpiry` gains a `Homedir` option (checks the same isolated keyring the signature is verified against, not a stale ambient copy) and now actually compares a key's expiry timestamp against the current time — previously it only checked that an expiry field was *present*, so an already-expired key was silently accepted. This is a real behavior fix on the already-shipped outbound email-signing path (`internal/pgp/sign.go`'s two callers).
- **`pgp.RanToCompletion`**: one shared, exhaustive-by-construction primitive (`nil` or `*exec.ExitError` = process ran to completion; everything else = operational failure) replacing three independent, incomplete `*exec.Error`-only checks that had already been patched piecemeal twice in this file before being consolidated.
- Docs: `docs/gpg-signature-verification.md` (new design doc, DES-034 in `DESIGN.md`), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `prfaq.tex`, `docs/README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` all updated to match shipped reality.

`VerifySignature` has **zero callers** by design — wiring it into the daemon's command-file loader (`LoadCommands`/`loadCommand`) is deferred to the headless GPG email agent epic (beadle-9zh), named explicitly in the design doc's migration plan.

## Why

`ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Zero agent authority" invariant requires every daemon action to come from a GPG-signed owner instruction. The stub made that invariant unenforceable — anything trusting its `nil` return was trusting nothing. This PR makes the verifier real without wiring it into a live path yet, so the trust-model work and the daemon-integration work can be reviewed and shipped as separate, appropriately-scoped units.

## Verification playbook

`VerifySignature` has no live entry point yet (by design), so verification is the real-gpg test suite, not a CLI/MCP demo — every test drives an actual `gpg` subprocess (ephemeral keypairs under `/tmp/bg-*`, real signing, real verification, real expiry via `seconds=N` keys and `sleep`), never mocked.

- `make check` — golangci-lint (0 issues), govulncheck (clean), markdownlint (0 errors), `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (all packages green).
- Invalid input: `TestVerifySignature_InvalidFingerprintFormat` — a malformed `ownerKeyID` (short ID, email, garbage) is rejected before any gpg call.
- Missing dependency: `TestVerifySignature_MissingGPGBinary` / `TestCheckKeyExpiry_MissingGPGBinary` / three exec-start-failure and permission-denied tests across `signature.go`'s call sites — a genuinely-absent or non-executable `gpg` binary surfaces as an unwrapped operational error, never misclassified as a signature verdict.
- Boundary: `TestCheckKeyExpiry_Expired` (a `seconds=3` key, slept past expiry, real gpg round-trip) and `TestVerifyDetachedSignature_ExpiredKey` (the same, driven through gpg's actual `EXPKEYSIG` status line) both prove the "key has expired" case end to end, at both of the two places it can be caught.
- Local review: `code-reviewer`, `silent-failure-hunter`, and `type-design-analyzer` all run on the full diff (twice, after the first round's findings were fixed); zero material findings remain.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check` passes clean
- [x] Every `SignatureReason` covered end-to-end against real gpg (success, missing, wrong-key, key-expired via two independent paths, invalid/tampered)
- [x] Coverage audit closed real gaps (`go tool cover` driven, not estimated)
- [x] Full-diff local review (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, type-design-analyzer) clean after two rounds
- [x] Operator confirmation: N/A — no live entry point exists yet (deferred to beadle-9zh); this is the one exception WORKFLOW.md's verification gate names for a change with no reachable entry point

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1

echo "sleeping past expiry..."

echo "=== list-keys after old subkey expired ==="

echo "=== attempt to sign now (only expired subkey exists) ==="

set -e
HOME_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/bg-XXXX)/g

FPR=$(gpg --batch --no-tty --list-keys --with-colons rot@example.com | awk -F: '/^fpr/{print $10; exit}')
echo "FPR=$FPR"

# Old signing subkey, short-lived, will expire.

sleep 5

echo "sign exit: $?"
cat /tmp/sign.err
echo "=== signature packet info (which key signed) ==="
